title: Dot product and projection (similarity)
summary: The dot product has a picture: the shadow (projection) of one arrow on the line through the other, multiplied by the other's length. The shadow is long when the arrows agree, zero at a right angle and negative when they point apart, and with unit vectors it is the cosine of the angle.
llm_link: Attention scores are dot products: each token's query vector is dotted with every other token's key vector, and a long shadow means that token gets listened to. Embedding search ranks documents by the same shadow, scaled to unit length (cosine similarity).
key_ideas: Projection of v onto w: the length of v's shadow on the line through w, light shining at right angles to that line.
v · w = (shadow of v on w) × |w|. Same direction: large and positive; perpendicular: 0; more than 90° apart: negative.
Why multiply-and-add works: shadows add, so v · w = x(î · w) + y(ĵ · w) = x·w₁ + y·w₂.
If |w| = 1 the dot product is the shadow itself; with both arrows of length 1 it is cos θ, which is why cosine similarity divides by both lengths.
proj = (v·w / w·w) w, and the leftover v − proj is perpendicular to w (the fact behind least squares).

quiz.q: v = [3, 4] and w = [1, 0]. How long is v's shadow on the line through w?
quiz.explain: w points along the x-axis and has length 1, so the shadow is just v's x-step: v · w / |w| = 3 / 1 = 3.
2·(−1) + 1·2 = 0. The arrows are at a right angle, so the shadow of one on the other has no length.

quiz.q: The dot product of two vectors is negative. What does that say about them?
options: One of them has negative length
They are more than 90° apart, so the shadow falls behind the origin
quiz.explain: Lengths are never negative; the sign comes from the shadow. When v turns more than a right angle away from w, its shadow lands on the far side of the origin.

quiz.q: Why does cosine similarity divide v · w by |v| |w|?
options: So that only direction matters: the result becomes the shadow of one unit arrow on another, cos θ
Because the dot product is otherwise always positive
To turn it into a distance
quiz.explain: Dividing by both lengths is the same as shrinking both arrows to length 1 first. Then the shadow is exactly cos θ, and a long document is not favoured just for being long.

quiz.q: In attention, a query q = [1, 0] is compared with keys k₁ = [0.9, 0.1], k₂ = [0, 1], k₃ = [−1, 0]. Which key gets the highest raw score q · k?
quiz.explain: The scores are 0.9, 0 and −1. k₁ points almost along q, so its shadow on q is longest; k₂ is perpendicular (0) and k₃ points the opposite way (negative).

problems.title: Project one vector onto another
problems.prompt:
Write dot(v, w) and project(v, w) for plain Python lists.

project returns the shadow of v on the line through w, as a vector: (v·w / w·w) · w. Projecting onto the zero vector makes no sense, so raise ValueError if w is all zeros.

project([2, 1], [-1, 2])  # [0.0, 0.0]  (perpendicular)
project([1, 3], [1, 1])   # [2.0, 2.0]

tests.name: dot works
tests.code:
out = dot([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6])
assert out == 32, f'expected 1*4 + 2*5 + 3*6 = 32, got {out}'

tests.name: onto an axis
tests.code:
out = project([2, 2], [3, 0])
assert out is not None, 'project returned None. Did you forget return?'
assert [round(x, 9) for x in out] == [2, 0], f'the shadow of [2, 2] on the x-axis is [2, 0], got {out}. Did you divide by w·w, not by |w|?'

tests.name: perpendicular gives zero
tests.code:
out = project([2, 1], [-1, 2])
assert all(abs(x) < 1e-12 for x in out), f'[2, 1] and [-1, 2] are at a right angle, so the shadow is [0, 0]; got {out}'

tests.name: general case
tests.code:
out = project([1, 3], [1, 1])
assert all(abs(a - b) < 1e-9 for a, b in zip(out, [2, 2])), f'expected [2.0, 2.0] (v·w = 4, w·w = 2, so 2 copies of w); got {out}'

tests.name: length of w does not matter
tests.code:
a = project([1, 3], [1, 1]); b = project([1, 3], [5, 5])
assert all(abs(x - y) < 1e-9 for x, y in zip(a, b)), f'projecting onto [1,1] and [5,5] must give the same shadow (same line), got {a} and {b}. Divide by w·w so the length of w cancels'

tests.name: zero vector is rejected

hints: dot: return sum(a * b for a, b in zip(v, w))
The shadow vector points along w, so it is some number k times w. k = dot(v, w) / dot(w, w).
raise ValueError("...") is the syntax: ValueError is called like a function.

problems.title: Shadow plus leftover
problems.prompt:
Write split(v, w) that returns a pair (along, leftover): along is the projection of v onto w, and leftover = v − along.

The tests check the two facts from the video: the pieces add back up to v, and the leftover is perpendicular to w (its dot product with w is 0).

tests.name: returns two vectors
tests.code:
out = split([3, 1], [1, 1])
assert out is not None and len(out) == 2, f'expected a pair (along, leftover), got {out}'

tests.name: pieces add back to v
tests.code:
along, left = split([3, 1], [1, 1])
s = [a + b for a, b in zip(along, left)]
assert all(abs(x - y) < 1e-9 for x, y in zip(s, [3, 1])), f'along + leftover should rebuild v = [3, 1], got {s}'

tests.name: leftover is perpendicular to w
tests.code:
along, left = split([3, 1], [1, 1])
d = sum(a * b for a, b in zip(left, [1, 1]))
assert abs(d) < 1e-9, f'leftover · w should be 0 (a right angle), got {d}. Is leftover = v - along, and not along - v or v - w?'

tests.name: works in 3D
tests.code:
along, left = split([1, 2, 3], [0, 0, 2])
assert all(abs(x - y) < 1e-9 for x, y in zip(along, [0, 0, 3])), f'the shadow of [1,2,3] on the z-axis is [0,0,3], got {along}'
assert all(abs(x - y) < 1e-9 for x, y in zip(left, [1, 2, 0])), f'the leftover should be [1,2,0], got {left}'

hints: leftover = [a - b for a, b in zip(v, along)]
return along, leftover returns a tuple of two lists.

problems.title: Attention scores in one line (NumPy, shape drill)
problems.prompt:
A query q has shape (d,). The keys are stacked as the rows of a matrix K with shape (n, d): one row per token.

tests.name: one score per key
tests.code:
import numpy as np
K = np.array([[0.9, 0.1], [0., 1.], [-1., 0.]]); q = np.array([1., 0.])
out = scores(q, K)
assert out is not None, 'scores returned None'
out = np.asarray(out)
assert out.shape == (3,), f'3 keys should give 3 scores, shape (3,); got shape {out.shape}. Did you compute q @ K or K.T @ q?'
assert np.allclose(out, [0.9, 0., -1.]), f'expected [0.9, 0, -1], got {out}'

tests.name: shape (n, d) @ (d,) is (n,)
tests.code:
import numpy as np
K = np.arange(12.).reshape(4, 3); q = np.array([1., 0., -1.])
out = np.asarray(scores(q, K))
assert out.shape == (4,), f'K is (4, 3) and q is (3,), so K @ q is (4,); got {out.shape}'
assert np.allclose(out, [-2., -2., -2., -2.]), f'each row a, b, c gives a - c = -2; got {out}'

tests.name: best picks the longest shadow
tests.code:
import numpy as np
K = np.array([[0., 1.], [2., 0.1], [1., 1.]]); q = np.array([1., 0.])
out = best(q, K)
assert out == 1, f'scores are [0, 2, 1], so key 1 wins; got {out}'
assert isinstance(out, int), f'return a Python int (int(np.argmax(...))), got {type(out).__name__}'

hints: np.array([K[i] @ q for i in range(len(K))]) works. So does K @ q: each row of K is dotted with q.
